propositions: Accepted /rerun and recheck-review requests exist only in the process-local asyncio queue and are lost if the receiver exits before dequeue, leaving the revision with a stale Gerrit vote and matching SQLite dedup row that causes reconciliation to skip it.

The repair writes exactly LLM-Review: 0 to the exact revision before acknowledging acceptance, creating a durable patchset-bearing comment-added event marker in the Gerrit events-log that reconciliation can consume after restart.

Reconciliation must query Gerrit before consulting local dedup; a successful no-nonzero-vote result clears the exact stale dedup row and proceeds to vote, while a Gerrit error preserves dedup and holds the cursor for retry.

Reset and verification must complete before acknowledgement; if reset fails, verification reads a surviving nonzero vote, or the retry budget cannot be cleared, the request is rejected without queuing a forced event.
Contributor text cannot select a label value or mint PASS/BLOCK; only the privileged reset operation writes a fixed neutral value, and affirmative/refusal replies remain provably label-free.

A stateful restart test proves that after discarding the old queue and retaining stale dedup, one reconciliation pass consumes the reset-emitted event and casts exactly one new vote for the same change/revision.
